notes.1: The best solutions showed clear working, starting from z3 in exponential form with the correct argument, and listed all three roots in the required form.
notes.2a: This part was done well, with most candidates stating the correct derivatives and dividing the second derivative by 2 to obtain the coefficient ofx2.
notes.2b: The majority of candidates used the formula for the integral of secx given in the list of formulae (MF19). A few candidates derived an incorrect formula or used a calculator without showing working.
notes.3a: This part of the question was well done with better responses showing full working when factorising det ( A−λI ) .
notes.3b: Better solutions maintained accuracy and used correct notation when manipulating the characteristic equation. Some candidates substituted in for A2 and I, which was not required to answer the question.
notes.4a: The majority of candidates found the first derivative correctly using parametric differentiation.
notes.4b: Attempts to find the second derivative varied in length. The best solutions showed the required level of algebraic fluency and did not omit to divide by after differentiating with respect to t.
notes.5: The majority of candidates divided both sides of the equation by x2+7x and found the integrating factor correctly by using partial fractions or completing the square. After multiplying both sides of the equation by x ( x+7 )−1 , the best answers appliedx = x+7−7 or integration by parts in order to integrate the right-hand side. They also maintained accuracy when substituting in the initial conditions.
notes.6a: Better solutions started by forming a correct expression for the sum of the areas of the rectangles. They proceeded to apply laws of logarithms clearly and finished by fully justifying the given answer.
notes.6b: Some candidates spotted that there weren−1 terms and so worked with nn−1, which led to a correct lower bound. A few candidates spotted that the difference between U and L is ln2, n n n which they used to reach a correct solution for this part of the question and the next part.
notes.6c: The best solutions showed enough working to justify that the difference between U and L is n n proportional to , hence justifying the given limit.
notes.7a: Almost all candidates knew how to approach this question and completed it to a high standard. The majority of them took the most efficient approach of substituting y =k to find the particular integral. There was some inaccuracy when solving linear equations to find the values of the constants and some problems with notation were seen. A few candidates gave expressions instead of equations as their answer.
notes.7b: Those who were successful with part (a) usually demonstrated the skills to derive and solve an equation of the form sinhax =b, and so were successful with this part also.
notes.8a: Almost all candidates recognised the integral as − +C, although it was common to see the n+1 arbitrary constant omitted.
notes.8b: The best solutions carried out integration by parts first, using the result from part (a) to inform their choice of parts. They then replaced cos2θ with 1−sin2θ to derive the given reduction formula successfully. The few candidates who applied cos2θ=1 −sin2θ first, before integrating by parts, or who split the product as sinm−1θcosnθsinθ were usually successful also.
notes.8c: After expanding z+z−1 using the binomial expansion, better responses grouped together terms clearly before applying the identity zn +z−n =2cosnθ to fully justify their answer.
notes.8d: This part was well done with the majority of candidates applying the reduction formula accurately.
notes.key_messages:
• Candidates should show all the steps in their solutions, particularly when proving a given result.
• Candidates should read questions carefully so that they answer all aspects in adequate depth, noting
when an answer is required in a certain form or in terms of a given variable.
• Candidates should make use of results derived in earlier parts of a question or given in the list of
formulae (MF19).
notes.general_comments:
There were many responses of a very high standard. The majority of candidates demonstrated very good
knowledge across the whole syllabus and showed their working clearly. In their handling of algebra and
calculus, they were accurate, and they also displayed understanding of linear algebra. It seemed that all
candidates were able to complete the paper in the time allowed.
Sometimes candidates did not justify their answers fully. This is particularly important where answers are
given within the question.
